title: Tela: A Temporal Load-Aware Cloud Virtual Disk Placement Scheme
problem: Cloud Virtual Disk (CVD) placement algorithms for Cloud Block Storage do not account for temporal load fluctuations, leading to imbalanced storage warehouse loads, low resource utilization, and frequent overloads under dynamic workloads.
motivation: Cloud storage loads are inherently time-varying, and static placement ignores this, causing hotspots that degrade I/O performance and waste physical storage capacity in data centers.
method: Tela predicts how I/O load patterns (the read/write traffic over time) will vary for each storage warehouse, rather than just looking at current conditions. It then places cloud virtual disks (CVD—chunks of data storage that live on physical hardware) onto warehouses in a way that spreads the workload both now and into the future, avoiding placements that would later overload a warehouse.
key_novelty: The key idea is using predictions of how load will change over time when deciding where to place virtual disks, so storage warehouses stay balanced over time rather than just at one moment.
contributions: Characterization of temporal load fluctuations in cloud storage and their impact on placement quality
Design of Tela, a placement scheme that models future load trajectories for storage warehouses
Demonstration of improved load balance, resource utilization, and reduced overload frequency compared to prior static placement methods

metrics.other: improved load balance and reduced overload frequency (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: prior CVD placement schemes that ignore temporal load variation
limitations: Specific performance numbers and validation methodology are not available from the abstract alone.
